$comment: The one place published names, the engine's Nx project and directory, the NAPI platform rows and the publish switches are declared. Workflows, scripts and tests read this file; rename here and nowhere else. A row's `container` is the pinned image its producer builds in (a Linux row builds in manylinux for its glibc floor); `floor` is an extra consumer cell that installs the candidate on the oldest supported distribution.

wasm.$comment: Spike: macos-latest is a hosted arm64 macOS label that no platform row uses, so the WASM build gets its own producer row and runs beside the native build. The selected delivery recipe still pins Darwin ARM64 host tools (emsdk, nightly rustc). Geospec CI runs on hosted runners only from 2026-10-17 (tau-cloud GEOSPEC_RUNNER_ROUTE=hosted).

ci.$comment: A platform row's `selfHosted` runner replaces its hosted `runner` (and every job on that hosted label) only for trusted events: a push or workflow_dispatch on main and, while `selfHostedPullRequests` is on, a pull request whose head is this repository and whose actor and author are not dependabot[bot]. Fork and Dependabot pull requests always stay on the hosted runner. `scripts/ci-plan.mjs` decides the route once per run. Off: the `local-mac-trusted` runner group (tau-cloud `stacks/repo/geospec`) admits only `ci.yml@refs/heads/main`, because a runner group cannot tell a same-repository pull request ref from a fork's.

publish.$comment: npm is on: the trusted-publisher bindings for ci.yml + npm-publish exist (2026-10-13), so every main push publishes a next prerelease. PyPI is on for stable releases only: an exact release commit publishes its wheels after the release pull request passed qualification. A main push never publishes to PyPI; its wheels carry the PEP 440 .devN form of the next version and only pass the dry run's twine check.
